currentFormalOrder: if fundamentalCount>=3 and fundamentalScore<25 => reject fundamental-quality
findings: financialDataCount() and fundamentalScore() use the same nine availability slots; the count gate is an availability prerequisite for the score, not an independent economic factor.
Current parseMopsIncomeHtml requires positive revenue plus numeric EPS, gross and operating values before a company-period row is admitted.
Current deriveQuarterlyFinancials requires latest, previous and same-quarter-last-year quarter reconstructions, each with positive quarter revenue.
A clean canonical quarterly FINANCIAL entry therefore supplies six countable slots by itself: revenueQoQ, eps, grossMargin, operatingMargin, grossMarginYoY and operatingMarginYoY.
Therefore fundamentalCount<3 is structurally unreachable on an uncorrupted canonical quarterly-financial row under current producer semantics.

The gate is still meaningful as a data-integrity fallback for alternate/custom/legacy merged rows. The preceding FINANCIAL_SOURCE_COMPLETENESS bundle can be satisfied by quarterRevenue + financialBasis + revenueQoQ + revenueQuarterYoY without supplying three of the nine fundamental-score slots.

The nullish revenueMoM ?? revenueQoQ alias can suppress a valid QoQ fallback when revenueMoM is non-null but nonnumeric; this state is technically feasible on permissive alternate enrichment and should be labeled provenance/invariant risk rather than ordinary fundamental weakness.

fixedCounterexamples.consequence: Earlier completeness can pass while count<3 rejects if the row is not the canonical quarterly producer shape.
Nullish selection chooses the invalid non-null MoM before toNumber(), so the valid QoQ fallback is lost.
